intro: If you want to explore the Sam Chuk 100-Year Market and sleep somewhere quiet and close to nature, Klindinaitawan Resort Samchuk is a small bungalow resort in Nong Phak Nak, Sam Chuk, surrounded by rice fields. What guests agree on most is a peaceful setting, clean rooms, a warm, hands-on owner, breakfast included and free parking — all from around ฿840/night. It's no luxury resort, but it has a relaxed, country-garden feel at a price that's easy on the wallet.

body.html: Klindinaitawan Resort Samchuk sits at 2/2 Moo 7, Nong Phak Nak, Sam Chuk — about 4-5 km from the Sam Chuk district centre and set out among the rice fields, away from the town, quiet and open. The resort is a cluster of small bungalows spread across a garden plot, with around 15 rooms ranging from single and twin to three-bed and family rooms. What reviewers love is the calm and the space to wander — ideal for anyone who wants to escape the bustle and sleep to the sounds of nature.

The rooms earn praise for being clean and simple in a way that just works. Each has air-conditioning, a TV, a fridge, a wardrobe, drinking water and an en-suite bathroom. Many guests say the rooms are well kept for the price, the beds are comfortable, and opening the door gives you a view of green rice paddies. Because they're separate bungalows, privacy is higher than a typical block hotel — a good fit for couples or families who want their own space.
"So peaceful. We woke up to green rice fields, the room was clean, the owner was kind, and breakfast was included — perfect for a relaxed, easygoing break."

What guests appreciate most is the friendly, personal care from the owner and team. Breakfast is served, there's free Wi-Fi, and parking on site. A garden and seating area let you sip a morning coffee in the breeze, and at times there are bikes to ride around the grounds. Overall it feels more like staying at a relative's country garden than a hotel — great for anyone who wants a warm, informal place to rest.

A few things to know before booking: it's out among the rice fields beyond the town, so a car is by far the easiest way to get around, as the shops and restaurants nearby aren't within walking distance. Nights are quiet and dark, so anyone who craves a lively scene might find it a little lonely. And because it borders the paddies, you may meet the odd insect in the rainy season or at dusk — pack some mosquito repellent to be comfortable.

Its Sam Chuk location suits travellers who've come specifically for the Sam Chuk 100-Year Market and the area's cultural sights. It's a short drive into the market for the old shophouses, temples and vintage cafés, before heading on to Bueng Chawak or the Don Chedi Monument the next day. Being out by the fields means you come back to genuine rest, with none of the city traffic noise.

The honest verdict from real reviews: Klindinaitawan Resort Samchuk is a rice-field bungalow stay that delivers quiet, privacy and warm hospitality on a budget — clean rooms, breakfast included, a friendly owner. You do have to accept that a car is really needed, the nights are very quiet, and there's the odd insect from the surrounding nature. But if you're visiting Sam Chuk and want to sleep close to nature in genuine calm, it's a worthwhile and memorable pick.

faqTitle: FAQ — Klindinaitawan Resort Samchuk Suphan Buri

faq.q: Where is Klindinaitawan Resort Samchuk, and how far is the Sam Chuk Market?
faq.a: It's at 2/2 Moo 7, Nong Phak Nak, Sam Chuk, Suphan Buri, out among the rice fields — about a 10-minute drive from the district centre and the Sam Chuk 100-Year Market. It's an out-of-town location with a quiet, peaceful feel, ideal for self-drivers who want to sleep close to nature and drive into the market the next day.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Klindinaitawan Resort Samchuk, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿840/night for a single room. There are also twin, three-bed and family rooms for larger groups. Breakfast is included. Rates vary by season and platform, so compare a few sites before booking.

faq.q: Who is Klindinaitawan Resort Samchuk best for?
faq.a: It's best for couples or families driving to Sam Chuk who want a quiet stay close to nature. They're separate bungalows by the rice fields — private, with breakfast and a friendly owner. It's less suited to anyone without a car, or anyone who wants a lively scene with shops within walking distance.

faq.q: Is there parking, and is breakfast included?
faq.a: There's free on-site parking and breakfast is served — since it's out of town with no walkable restaurants, having breakfast and parking helps a lot for self-drivers.

faq.q: Is the stay quiet and private, and are there many insects?
faq.a: These are separate bungalows by the rice fields, so it's genuinely quiet and private — great for a proper rest. Because it borders the paddies, you may meet the odd insect in the rainy season or at dusk — bring mosquito repellent so you can sit outside comfortably.
